Elijah — thank you for sharing and I'm glad you gave us the heads up. I appreciate the clinical note.

High level next steps I propose:
- Immediate: confirm formal leave dates with People Ops and get any required paperwork filed (Monica).
- Coverage: identify interim owners for your high-priority tasks and a point person for immediate customer escalations (Jonas/Marcus).
- Handover: you to provide a brief handover matrix (tasks, owners, runbooks, blockers) by end of day Friday 12/10.
- Check-ins: set a weekly check-in cadence for the first 4 weeks post-surgery to reassess workload and accommodations.

I’ll coordinate the handover meeting with the core team. Please confirm that People Ops can share the minimum necessary health info with your managers for accommodation planning. If you prefer, Monica can lead the paperwork and any occupational-health referral.

Would 11am PST on Fri 12/3 work for a quick 30-minute sync?

Thanks — we’ll make this as low-friction as possible.

Hi all — thanks for the note, Elijah, and Grace for the proposed plan. I’m People Ops business partner on this case; I’ll own the paperwork and the accommodation process. A few items from HR: 

- Please complete and return the short-term leave form (attached) so we can record official dates.
- If you’re open to it, we’ll schedule an occupational health consultation with Ashford Occupational Health to get a formal recommendation for phased duties and any ergonomic needs. They will only receive clinical info with your consent.
- I’ve attached the short-term-accommodation-guidelines.pdf which outlines typical options (reduced hours, no travel, remote-first for 4–6 weeks, temporary task reallocation).

Elijah — can you confirm: (a) the tentative last day you expect to be fully active, (b) any tasks you consider blockers if unassigned, and (c) your preferred interim contact for customers? Once I have the form back I’ll create a People Ops case and add the occupational health appointment.

I’ll be available on Fri 12/10 for the handover meeting; if that’s a hard deadline for the matrix, I’ll follow up with a short intake call beforehand.

- Handover matrix: Elijah to upload the completed handover_matrix_elijah_dec2026.xlsx to the shared folder by EOD Fri 12/10 (Action: Elijah).
- Interim owners:
  • Customer escalation & on-call for Model A inference regressions: Marcus Lin (primary) / Jonah B. from infra (backup).
  • Active performance optimization sprint: Jonas Weber to re-prioritize tasks and assign two ICs for critical path.
- Low-risk tasks: scheduled for deferral until return or assigned to Triage pool.
- Communication: Slack channel #team-inference to have a pinned post with status updates; Marcus to post daily for first 2 weeks.
- Access: Elijah retains read access to his repos; write access paused on 12/15 for safety until he confirms readiness (Action: IT via ticket; Marcus to open).
- Coverage budget: we’ll use contractor hours for weeks 2–4 if needed; finance checkbox complete (Jonas please confirm).

Escalation plan (if recovery extends beyond 8 weeks): quick decision tree — reassign long-running initiatives, consider temporary hire or extended contractor. We’ll aim to avoid blocking launches.

Please acknowledge you’ve taken the actions below and capture any missing items in the shared handover doc. I’ve attached a clean handover matrix template for Elijah to use.

Thanks — I’ll also join the intake call with Monica to represent the product team.

—
